themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Surge
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 4 reports this week compared to a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (967% increase, z-score 7.49), suggesting either new construction disturbances, building demolitions, or environmental contamination—a public health concern requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 asbestos complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (967% spike)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates statistical anomaly at highest severity level
1,341 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (215 new buildings, 36 full demolitions) creates exposure risk during construction/demolition activities
reporting_angles: Which specific construction or demolition sites triggered this week's asbestos complaints? Are contractors following EPA abatement protocols?
Are residents near active demolitions (including the 36 full demolitions tracked by DOB) being notified of asbestos risk and remediation timelines?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Pest Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints hit 10 reports this week versus 3.2 weekly average (208% spike, z-score 5.63), coupled with unsanitary pigeon complaints up 700% to 3 this week (vs. 0.4 baseline), suggesting a compounding sanitation and public health crisis.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints this week vs. 3.2 weekly average (208% spike, z-score 5.63)
3 unsanitary pigeon complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
688 dirty condition complaints over 90 days indicates broader sanitation baseline concerns
reporting_angles: Has DSNY or Parks Department increased rodent/pigeon abatement in Greenpoint/Williamsburg? If not, why are complaints spiking now?
Are dead animals clustered in specific neighborhoods (waterfront, parks, commercial zones)? Could indicate disease outbreak or food waste management failure.

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints doubled to 181 reports last week from 87 weekly average (108% spike, z-score 6.55)—the highest-ranking spike in frequency—suggesting new venues, events, or construction activity generating sustained disturbance.
evidence: 181 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 87 weekly baseline (108% increase, z-score 6.55)
Commercial noise is 3rd largest complaint category overall at 1,287 over 90 days, now accelerating
Community Board repeatedly requests 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety' suggesting ongoing quality-of-life friction with commercial activity
reporting_angles: Which specific venues (bars, restaurants, music venues, construction sites) are driving the spike? Are they newly opened or recently licensed?
Are 311 complaints being routed to NYPD for enforcement? What is the average response time and outcome?

themes_detail.label: Street Light Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints surged to 34 reports two weeks ago from 11.4 weekly average (199% spike, z-score 5.66), creating public safety and pedestrian access risks—especially concerning given CB's repeated requests for traffic and pedestrian safety improvements.
evidence: 34 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 11.4 weekly average (199% spike, z-score 5.66)
Community Board budget includes recurring request to 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety, including traffic calming' indicating historical infrastructure gaps
976 street condition complaints over 90-day period suggests broader municipal maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Is DOT prioritizing repairs in Greenpoint/Williamsburg? What is the average repair time for street light outages by neighborhood?
Are dark streets correlating with increased crime or accidents? Cross-reference with NYPD data and accident reports.

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Encampments Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 21 reports last week from 5.5 weekly average (282% spike, z-score 3.97), and Community Board repeatedly budgets for 'services for the homeless'—signaling either a growing visible homeless population or concentration in specific areas.
evidence: 21 encampment complaints last week vs. 5.5 weekly baseline (282% increase, z-score 3.97)
Community Board's annual budget request for 'other request for services for the homeless' suggests unmet demand and recurring crisis
Unleashed dog complaints also up 409% (7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.4 avg), possibly correlated with encampment presence
reporting_angles: Where are encampments concentrated (parks, waterfront, commercial districts)? Have they moved from other neighborhoods or grown in place?
Is DHS providing outreach and shelter capacity to address this surge? What services exist in CD 301 specifically?
